newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK post-1997 status to equal China province - report.
newsitem.headline: HK post-1997 status to equal China province - report.

text.p: Hong Kong would be equal to a Chinese province and its future leader would be equal to a senior Chinese minister, a regional magazine said on Thursday.
Britain hands the colony back to China at midnight on June 30 next year, and Beijing is now organising the selection of a chief executive to replace Governor Chris Patten.

Asiaweek quoted sources as saying Beijing had recently decided the status of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, as the territory will be known, would be equal to a province or central government ministry.

The chief executive would rank on a par with China's foreign or defence ministers or the leaders of big municipalities such as Beijing or Shanghai, who often sit on the ruling Communist Party's decision-making Politburo.
Asiaweek said this would also mean the chief executive would be more senior than the foreign and defence ministry representatives whom Beijing will station in Hong Kong after the handover.
